Forces belonging to Blackwater founder and Trump ally Erik Prince suffered a major defeat in eastern Congo on September 17, when an ambush left around 20 people dead or wounded.
At least seven Congolese and a former New Zealand special forces soldier were killed. 
Former UFC fighter and U.S. Green Beret Tim Kennedy was shot three times in the leg and is being treated at Walter Reed military hospital near Washington.
Three sources said the sophistication of the attack suggested involvement by Rwandan forces backing M23 rebels. One source said the attackers may have tracked a surveillance drone to the team's location.

🛢 Saudi Aramco claims to have restored full crude supplies to Europe after pipeline attack
Saudi Aramco has told European refiners it will provide full allocations of crude in November after the kingdom's East-West pipeline resumed operations following attacks, Bloomberg reported.
Last month, Aramco told European refiners they would be allocated no crude in October after the pipeline was hit.
Saudi Arabia typically exports 700,000–800,000 barrels per day to Europe. In the meantime, the vulnerability remains — just one Houthi missile could cause another critical disruption.

📉🛢 Oil prices dip a little amid Iran war speculation
Brent crude futures decreased by about 1% to under $103 per barrel after Trump proclaimed that the US won’t resume attacks on Iran before the midterms next month, Reuters reported.
During the previous session, before Trump’s announcement, Brent prices rose by about 4%.
